g11-geography-ug2-t1.overview: Criteria for Climate Classification sits inside Climate Classification and Climate Regions of Our World. Climate classification is the focus of Unit 2 of Grade 11 Geography in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it sets out the criteria that geographers use to sort climates, then it works through Köppen’s system and its modified Köppen-Geiger version. Next it maps the low-latitude, mid-latitude, and high-latitude regions, the factors that shape them, and Ethiopia’s own Bereha-to-Wurch zones, and it leads into Unit 3: Natural Resources and Conflicts over Resources. Students will also learn how climate classification applies to real-life situations.

g11-geography-ug2-t1.simple:
Criteria for Climate Classification in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, the ancient Greek zones of Frigid, Temperate, and Torrid, which reflect sunlight and habitability.
  • The difference between genetic schemes, which follow the forces that drive climate, and empirical schemes.
  • Then how temperature, precipitation, and natural vegetation feed a workable climate classification.
  • Also the strengths of Köppen’s and Trewartha’s methods for wide, data-rich regions.
